newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian currency design talks hit new snag.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian currency design talks hit new snag.

text.p: Talks on the design of a joint currency for Bosnia are beginning to resemble protracted peace negotiations between rival leaders during the country's war.

Western officials said on Friday that Serb representatives refused principles proposed by international mediators for the design of an interim currency. Leaders of the Moslem-Croat federation agreed to the principles.
Agreement between Bosnia's Serb, Croat and Moslem leaders on the currency design is the last obstacle for a stand-by arrangement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

Although the IMF has not set any deadlines, the international community has linked the IMF deal with Bosnia's upcoming fund-raising conference in July, which should bring $1.4 billion in funds for reconstruction in 1997.

International High representative Carlos Westendorp asked the Serb member of the country's collective presidency, Momcilo Krajisnik, to respond to design principles proposed by French governor of the central bank Serge Robert and IMF.

Presidency chairman, Alija Izetbegovic, a Moslem, and Croat member Kresimir Zubak immediately agreed to the proposal but Krajisnik's signature was needed as well because presidency decisions require a consensus.
"We are disappointed by Mr.Krajisnik's response to the question of design of the currency," spokesman Simon Haselock told Reuters.
Haselock said the High Representative planned to press the issue with Krajisnik so it could be resolved in time for the donors' conference.
"We will continue to engage with him, and we hope that it won't call into question our intention to hold the donors' conference towards the end of this month," he said.
